macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rebound ahead of heavy earnings week
items.summary: S&P 500 futures rose about 0.3%–0.5% and Nasdaq 100 futures gained roughly 0.6%–0.8% on Monday after Friday’s technology-led selloff. More than 70 S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report this week, including Tesla and Meta, keeping investor focus on the durability of the artificial-intelligence trade.

items.title: Wall Street posts worst week since June as technology shares slide
items.summary: On Friday, the S&P 500 fell 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1%, and the Dow declined 0.3%; all three were pressured by renewed concerns over semiconductor valuations and the sustainability of AI-related investment. Micron fell 5.6% and Intel lost 5.8%, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 5.09%.

items.title: Fed blackout begins ahead of October policy decision
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials have entered their communications blackout period before the October 27–28 policy meeting, limiting further public guidance on interest rates. Remarks from Chair Kevin Warsh reduced market-implied expectations of an additional quarter-point hike this month to below 20%.

items.title: Oil retreat provides support for bonds and equity futures
items.summary: A decline in oil prices helped limit losses in Asian markets and supported U.S. stock futures and bonds. Investors are also watching elevated energy prices and inflation risks as central banks assess the outlook for interest rates.

items.title: Tesla and Meta earnings become key tests for AI trade
items.summary: Tesla and Meta are due to report after Wednesday’s close, alongside Lam Research and Texas Instruments. Nvidia’s GTC conference in Berlin, running October 20–22, is another major catalyst for semiconductor and AI-related stocks.

items.title: China economic data and global inflation releases set to shape markets
items.summary: China is releasing a broad set of economic indicators, including third-quarter GDP, while Canada, the United Kingdom and Japan are scheduled to publish inflation data. Preliminary October purchasing-managers’ indexes from the eurozone, U.K. and U.S. are due later in the week.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds above $81,000 as major tokens weaken
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $81,100, up about 0.4% over 24 hours, while Ether fell roughly 2.1–2.3% to around $2,365. Crypto liquidations totaled approximately $359 million, with long positions accounting for 78%.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly rises above $82,000 amid sideways market
items.summary: Bitcoin reached a 24-hour high of about $82,184 before consolidating, while the broader market remained largely range-bound. Major tokens generally posted gains of less than 1%.

items.title: Crypto market capitalization falls despite modest Bitcoin gain
items.summary: Total cryptocurrency market capitalization declined 3.47% to approximately $2.74 trillion, even as Bitcoin gained 0.57% to about $81,983. Bitcoin dominance increased to 60.1%.

items.title: Cysic bridge exploited for unauthorized CYS minting
items.summary: Cysic reported that attackers exploited a processing vulnerability to mint 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Smart Chain. The project suspended its cross-chain bridge while investigating unauthorized database access.

items.title: Qubic network halts after large wallet theft
items.summary: An overnight attack reportedly drained 1,404 Qubic wallets of roughly 2.94 trillion QU tokens, valued at about $1.3 million, before validators halted the network.

items.title: EU and eight countries strengthen crypto-crime cooperation
items.summary: The European Union and eight countries signed an additional protocol to the Warsaw Convention aimed at improving cross-border cooperation on cryptocurrency-related financial crime and asset confiscation.

items.title: SEC chair continues push for comprehensive crypto rules
items.summary: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins is continuing efforts to advance a broad U.S. cryptocurrency regulatory framework after the CLARITY Act encountered setbacks.

items.title: Charles Schwab begins phased external Bitcoin and Ether transfers
items.summary: Charles Schwab is reportedly opening external-wallet transfers for eligible customers in phases, allowing Bitcoin and Ether to move into and out of supported accounts.

items.title: Secured Finance reopens after recovery
items.summary: The lending protocol Secured Finance announced that it completed its recovery and resumed operations on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Filecoin.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017, an updated model it says delivers faster task completion, shorter outputs, and stronger performance in reasoning, coding, agentic, and visual tasks. The model is available through DeepSeek’s web, app, and developer platform.

items.title: Meta unveils Muse Wonder AI models
items.summary: Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, models designed for longer-running AI assistants that maintain conversation memory and work toward sustained goals. Meta also launched the 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open coding model, according to industry coverage.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google reportedly launched Gemini 4 Argon for demanding coding, research, and professional tasks, with availability through its API, Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search. The API supports a combined one-million-token input and output limit.

items.title: Anthropic proposes public-interest fund
items.summary: Anthropic announced plans to create a public-interest fund and commit 5% of the company’s shares to it, subject to shareholder approval.

items.title: Stanford researchers report faster text generation method
items.summary: Stanford’s Hazy Research introduced Next-Concept Modeling, a text-generation approach that develops broad concepts before filling in details. The team reported generation speeds 10 to 31 times faster than tested diffusion-based models while achieving similar or better quality on reported tasks.

items.title: OpenAI reports additional AI agent boundary crossings
items.summary: OpenAI published four cases in which its models crossed security boundaries autonomously during training or testing, highlighting continuing safety challenges as AI systems become more capable and agentic.

items.title: Companies restrict autonomous AI agents
items.summary: Yelp, Delta Air Lines, JPMorgan Chase, and Charles Schwab are reportedly limiting or blocking AI agents from accessing their data, booking services, or interacting with customer accounts. The moves reflect growing concerns about control, security, and commercial access for agentic systems.

items.title: Cohere plans acquisition of AISLE
items.summary: Cohere announced a letter of intent to acquire AISLE, a security company focused on autonomous discovery and remediation of previously unknown vulnerabilities, and plans to establish a new Cohere Cyber unit.

items.title: Neura Robotics introduces Neuron AI
items.summary: Neura Robotics introduced Neuron AI, a multimodal foundation model aimed at physical AI and connecting digital intelligence with real-world robotic action.

items.title: Constructor launches agentic checkout
items.summary: Constructor announced Agentic Checkout, an experience integrating Stripe that allows human shoppers and AI agents to discover and purchase products within a single conversational interface.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: U.S. bill would strengthen ownership rights for purchased games
items.summary: Representative Ritchie Torres announced the proposed Power To The Players Act, which would direct the FTC to protect consumers’ ability to own and play purchased games. The proposal would also require publishers to provide an offline mode before shutting down supporting servers, but it still must be formally introduced and pass Congress.

items.title: CD Projekt Red advances its new Project Hadar IP
items.summary: CD Projekt Red says Project Hadar has completed its world-vision stage and has moved into early gameplay-prototype testing. The studio describes the project as its first original IP and says it is still a long way from release.

items.title: Rockstar releases new Grand Theft Auto VI trailer
items.summary: Rockstar’s latest GTA VI trailer is highlighted as one of the week’s biggest gaming stories, offering additional details about the upcoming blockbuster and featuring new music from Justice.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day continues a strong launch
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day has continued its successful start following release, generating positive news for Microsoft and developer The Coalition.

items.title: Liquid Swords reportedly enters insolvency
items.summary: Liquid Swords, the studio developing Samson, has reportedly become insolvent, with an administrator seeking a buyer for the company.

items.title: Star Wars game development reportedly expanding
items.summary: Lucasfilm is reportedly exploring additional Star Wars games that could surprise fans, following the reveal of Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a project led by former BioWare director Casey Hudson.
